name: Angkor Wat
blurb: The world's largest religious monument and Cambodia's national symbol.

name: Bayon Temple
nameKh: ប្រាសាទបាយ័ន
blurb: Two hundred serene stone faces at the exact center of Angkor Thom.

name: Ta Prohm
nameKh: ប្រាសាទតាព្រហ្ម
blurb: A monastery left in the grip of silk-cotton roots, deliberately unrestored.

name: Banteay Srei
nameKh: ប្រាសាទបន្ទាយស្រី
blurb: Pink sandstone cut so finely the carvings still read a thousand years on.

name: Koh Ker
nameKh: កោះកេរ្តិ៍
blurb: A capital for only twenty years, and a seven-tier pyramid to prove it.
detail: Built for Suryavarman II in the first half of the twelfth century as a state temple and, unusually, dedicated to Vishnu rather than Shiva. It is oriented west, which is why sunrise is watched from in front of it rather than behind. The outer gallery carries around 600 metres of continuous bas-relief — the Churning of the Sea of Milk on the east wing is the one most people come back for. The temple was never fully abandoned after Angkor's fall, which is why it survived in better condition than most of the city around it.

name: Sambor Prei Kuk
nameKh: សំបូរព្រៃគុក
blurb: Pre-Angkorian brick towers of Ishanapura, older than Angkor by three centuries.

name: Royal Palace
nameKh: ព្រះបរមរាជវាំង
blurb: The working residence of the monarchy, and the Silver Pagoda beside it.

name: National Museum
nameKh: សារមន្ទីរជាតិ
blurb: The largest collection of Khmer sculpture, held in a terracotta pavilion.

name: Preah Vihear Temple
nameKh: ប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារ
blurb: A temple laid along an 800-metre axis on the cliff edge of the Dangrek range.

name: Spean Praptos
nameKh: ស្ពានព្រះប្ដោស
blurb: The longest surviving Angkorian corbel-arch bridge, still carrying traffic after eight hundred years.

name: Angkorian Royal Road
nameKh: ផ្លូវរាជបុរាណអង្គរ
blurb: The 225 km highway east from Angkor to Bakan, with its bridges, fire houses, and hospital chapels.

name: Preah Khan of Kompong Svay
nameKh: ប្រាសាទព្រះខ័នកំពង់ស្វាយ
blurb: The largest temple enclosure the Khmer empire ever walled, with one of its best-preserved hospital chapels.

name: Phnom Kulen
blurb: The sacred mountain where the Khmer Empire was declared in 802 CE.

name: Banteay Chhmar
nameKh: បន្ទាយឆ្មារ
blurb: A vast Jayavarman VII temple city in the north-west, with a community homestay inside the village beside it.

name: Yeak Laom Crater Lake
blurb: A near-perfect volcanic crater held by the Tampuan community, clear enough to swim all year.

name: Bou Sra Waterfall
blurb: Two tiers dropping into Bunong forest, loudest at the end of the rains.
detail: Two tiers, roughly ten and twenty-five metres, dropping through Bunong forest near the Vietnamese border. A path and a small suspension bridge reach the lower fall, and the volume changes completely with the season — thunderous from September into November, and a fraction of that by March. The land around it is Bunong, and the entry fee goes to the community that holds it.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Sen Monorom & Bunong Villages
nameKh: សែនមនោរម្យ
blurb: The highland town and the villages around it, where Bunong is still the first language.

name: Virachey National Park
blurb: Multi-day ranger-led treks into one of the least-visited protected areas in the country.

name: Katieng & Kachanh Waterfalls
blurb: Two short rides out of Banlung, both with a path behind the curtain of water.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Ou Sean Lair Waterfall
blurb: A seven-tier fall on a rubber-estate road east of Banlung, quiet on a weekday.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Dak Dam Waterfall
blurb: A short walk through Bunong farmland to a fall most visitors never reach.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Banlung Market
blurb: Highland produce, backstrap weaving and the red dust the province is known for.

name: Kachon Kreung Village
blurb: A Kreung village on the Sesan, with carved cemetery figures in the forest behind it.

name: Andoung Meas Jarai Villages
blurb: Jarai settlements upriver towards the border, reached by boat from Voen Sai.

name: Ratanakiri Coffee Farms
blurb: Robusta and arabica grown on basalt soil, roasted and poured in Banlung.

name: Mondulkiri Coffee Plantations
blurb: Smallholder plots around Sen Monorom and Bou Sra, many of them Bunong-run.

name: Elephant Valley Project
blurb: Retired working elephants observed in forest rather than ridden, run with Bunong mahouts.

name: Phnom Prich Wildlife Sanctuary
blurb: Dry forest and grassland holding gaur, banteng and some of the last wild cattle herds.

name: Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary
blurb: Evergreen forest holding black-shanked douc and yellow-cheeked gibbon, with dawn gibbon treks from Andoung Kraloeng.

name: Lumphat Wildlife Sanctuary
blurb: Dry dipterocarp forest along the Srepok, and some of the best vulture watching left in the country.

name: Sesan & Srepok Rivers
nameKh: សេសាន និង ស្រែពក
blurb: The two highland rivers that carry the northeast down to the Mekong, run by longtail and kayak.

name: Ta Veng & the Upper Sesan
blurb: The put-in for Brao river villages and the northern gate into Virachey.

name: Phnom Doh Kromom
blurb: A hilltop pagoda above Banlung, and the province's standing sunset spot.

name: Phnom Nam Lyr
blurb: A forested massif on the Vietnamese border, held sacred locally and rarely climbed.

name: Kampong Phluk
nameKh: កំពង់ភ្លុក
blurb: Houses on ten-metre stilts, reached by boat through flooded mangrove.
detail: Three villages of stilt houses standing six to ten metres above the dry-season ground, which puts the floors just above the water at peak flood. In the wet months you arrive by motorboat and transfer to a rowing boat to go through the flooded forest; in the dry months the same route is a road, and the stilts are the whole point of the visit. Going with the village boat cooperative rather than a tour launch keeps the fare in Kampong Phluk.

name: Kampong Khleang
nameKh: កំពង់ឃ្លាំង
blurb: The largest lakeside settlement, and far quieter than the villages nearer town.

name: Chnok Tru
blurb: A whole town afloat at the southern end of the lake — shops, school and petrol station all on pontoons.

name: Me Chrey
blurb: The smallest of the Siem Reap villages, ringed by lotus in the months after the flood.

name: Chong Kneas
blurb: The closest landing to Siem Reap and the start of the boat crossing to Battambang.

name: Battambang – Siem Reap Boat
blurb: Eight hours down the Sangker and across the lake, the best way to read the whole system in a day.

name: Kampi Dolphin Pool
blurb: One of the last deep pools holding Irrawaddy dolphins on the Mekong.

name: Prek Toal Bird Sanctuary
blurb: The most important waterbird colony in South-East Asia, best at first light.

name: Ang Trapeang Thmor
nameKh: អាងត្រពាំងថ្ម
blurb: A Khmer Rouge-era reservoir turned reserve, and the country's most reliable sarus crane site.

name: Boeung Tonle Chhmar
nameKh: បឹងទន្លេឆ្មារ
blurb: A Ramsar site and biosphere core area on the north shore, with flooded forest still intact.

name: Koh Trong
blurb: A sandbank island opposite Kratié, circled in an hour by bicycle.
tips: Rent a bicycle at the pier

name: Koh Dach (Silk Island)
blurb: Silk looms under stilt houses, a short ferry from the edge of Phnom Penh.
tips: Rent a bicycle at the pier

name: Koh Paen & the Bamboo Bridge
blurb: A bamboo bridge rebuilt by hand every dry season, and washed away by every flood.
tips: Rent a bicycle at the pier

name: Koh Sotin
blurb: Sandbars, tobacco fields and a ferry crossing that has not changed much in decades.
tips: Rent a bicycle at the pier

name: Kandal Rice Plains
blurb: Paddy and lotus ponds on the floodplain either side of the capital.

name: Stung Sen Floodplain
blurb: Deepwater rice that grows with the flood, on the river feeding the lake's northern core area.

name: Kampong Chhnang Pottery Villages
nameKh: កំពង់ឆ្នាំង
blurb: The province is named for its cooking pots, still coil-built by hand and fired in the open.

name: Bon Om Touk (Water Festival)
nameKh: បុណ្យអុំទូក
blurb: Longboat racing on the river each November, when the Tonle Sap turns back around.

name: The Dai Fishery
blurb: Rows of stationary bag nets strung across the Tonle Sap river to meet the migration out of the lake.

name: Stung Treng Ramsar Site
blurb: Braided channels and seasonally flooded forest running north to the Lao border.

name: Tonle Sap Sunset Boats
blurb: The lake edge at the end of the day, when the fishing fleet goes out.
tips: Arrive early for a good spot

name: Wat Hanchey
nameKh: វត្តហាន់ជ័យ
blurb: A pre-Angkorian brick sanctuary on a bluff, with the Mekong laid out below it at dusk.
tips: Arrive early for a good spot

name: Phnom Sambok
blurb: A two-tier hilltop pagoda north of Kratié, reached by a staircase through the trees.
tips: Arrive early for a good spot

name: Central Cardamom Mountains
nameKh: ជួរភ្នំក្រវាញ
blurb: The largest rainforest left in mainland South-East Asia, and still being surveyed.

name: Phnom Samkos
blurb: The second summit of the country at 1,717 m, inside a wildlife sanctuary of the same name.

name: Phnom Kulen
blurb: The sandstone plateau Angkor was quarried from, with a riverbed of carved lingas near the top.

name: Bokor National Park
blurb: An abandoned hill station on a plateau that makes its own weather.

name: Botum Sakor National Park
blurb: A peninsula of mangrove, melaleuca and lowland forest between the Cardamoms and the sea.

name: Tatai Waterfall
blurb: A wide, low fall reached by boat up the Tatai river, swimmable outside the wet season.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Popokvil Falls
blurb: Two drops on the Bokor plateau, thunderous in September and dry by March.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Phnom Kulen Waterfalls
blurb: The falls on the sacred mountain, busy at weekends and empty on a weekday morning.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Kbal Chhay Waterfall
blurb: Three streams over sandstone shelves, half an hour inland from the coast.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Chambok Waterfall
blurb: A forty-metre fall at the end of a community-run trail on the edge of Kirirom.
tips: Strongest flow in the wet season

name: Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple
blurb: A seventh-century brick shrine standing inside a limestone cave, reached by ladder.

name: Kampong Trach Caves
nameKh: កំពង់ត្រាច
blurb: A collapsed karst hill you walk into, opening onto a sinkhole garden in the middle.

name: Phnom Sorsia
blurb: Two caves in one outcrop — one full of bats, one lit through a hole in the roof.

name: Phnom Aural
nameKh: ភ្នំឧរ៉ាល់
blurb: The highest peak in Cambodia at 1,813 m, a hard two-day climb with a guide.

name: Kbal Spean
nameKh: ក្បាលស្ពាន
blurb: A forty-minute climb through forest to a riverbed carved with a thousand lingas.

name: Areng Valley
blurb: A valley the community kept from being dammed, now walked rather than flooded.

name: Kirirom National Park
blurb: Pine forest cool enough to need a jacket, two hours from Phnom Penh.
tips: Nights can be cool in the highlands

name: Osoam Cardamom Community
blurb: A village centre deep in the range, and the usual base for multi-day walks into it.
tips: Nights can be cool in the highlands

name: Chi Phat
blurb: A former logging village turned trekking base, with mountain-bike routes cut by the community.
tips: Start early to beat the heat

name: Kampot – Kep Countryside Loop
blurb: Forty flat kilometres between pepper farms, salt pans and the karst outcrops.
tips: Start early to beat the heat

name: Phnom Sampeau
blurb: The bat cave empties in a ribbon at dusk, watched from the road below.

name: Phnom Banan
blurb: 358 steps to a five-towered hilltop temple, with the Sangker plain behind it.

name: Dangrek Escarpment
nameKh: ជួរភ្នំដងរែក
blurb: The cliff edge below Preah Vihear temple, with the plain running out 500 m underneath.

name: Phnom Bok
blurb: Six hundred steps to a ninth-century hilltop temple, and the plain at first light.

name: The Bokor Cloud Line
blurb: The altitude where the plateau's own weather forms, and the reason the hill station was built.

name: Koh Rong Sanloem
nameKh: កោះរុងសន្លឹម
blurb: Saracen Bay for the sand, Lazy Beach for the sunset, plankton after dark.
detail: The quieter of the two big islands, and effectively three separate places: Saracen Bay on the east with most of the accommodation, Lazy Beach over the ridge facing the sunset, and M'Pai Bay in the north with the island's small village. Walking between them takes twenty to forty minutes on forest paths. The bioluminescent plankton is real and best on a dark, moonless night away from the bay lights.

name: Koh Rong
blurb: The bigger, louder sister island, with jungle trails to empty beaches on the far side.

name: Koh Ta Kiev
blurb: Near-shore and barely developed — hammocks, generators and no road.

name: Koh Thmei
blurb: Inside Ream National Park, with mangrove channels instead of nightlife and birds instead of bars.

name: Koh Tonsay (Rabbit Island)
blurb: Twenty minutes off Kep, with a single beach and a row of wooden bungalows.

name: Koh Sdach Archipelago
blurb: A working fishing cluster off Botum Sakor, with reef between the islands and few visitors.

name: Koh Kong Island
blurb: Seven beaches on the country's largest island, an hour by boat and rarely busy.

name: Otres Beach
blurb: The long quiet strip south of Sihanoukville, best in the late afternoon.

name: Long Set (4K) Beach
blurb: Four kilometres of sand on Koh Rong's east coast, walkable from the pier in an hour.

name: Lazy Beach
blurb: The west-facing bay on Sanloem, reached over the ridge and pointed at the sunset.

name: Koh Seh Marine Reserve
blurb: A conservation base rebuilding seagrass and reef in the Kep archipelago.

name: Kep Seagrass Beds
blurb: The largest seagrass meadows left on the coast, and the nursery behind the crab you eat ashore.

name: Koh Tang Dive Sites
blurb: The clearest water in Cambodian waters, four hours offshore on a liveaboard.

name: Koh Prins Wrecks
blurb: Two wrecks in open water off the outer islands, the only wreck diving on this coast.

name: Sanloem Reef Snorkeling
blurb: Shallow coral off the north of the island, swimmable straight from the sand.

name: Koh Russei (Bamboo Island)
blurb: A small island close in, with reef at both ends and a shallow crossing between them.

name: Kep & the Crab Market
blurb: Crab straight off the boats, cooked with green Kampot pepper.

name: Psar Leu Seafood Market
blurb: The port's own market, where the day's catch lands before it reaches any restaurant.

name: Kampot Fish Market
blurb: A restored deco market hall on the quay, busiest when the estuary boats come in.

name: Peam Krasop Mangroves
blurb: A kilometre of boardwalk through standing mangrove, with a tower at the end.

name: Ream National Park
blurb: Mangrove channels, dry forest and two beaches, half an hour from the airport.

name: Kampot Estuary & Salt Fields
blurb: Salt pans worked by hand between the river mouth and the sea, flooded and dried by season.

name: Gulf Sunset Cruises
blurb: Evening sailings out through the archipelago, most leaving from Otres.

name: Kampot River Cruises
blurb: Slow boats up the Praek Tuek Chhu at dusk, with fireflies in the mangrove after dark.

name: Sisowath Quay
nameKh: មហាវិថីស៊ីសុវត្ថិ
blurb: The two-kilometre promenade along the Tonle Sap, at its best an hour before dark.

name: Wat Phnom & the Colonial Quarter
blurb: The hill the capital is named after, and the post office square and villas around it.

name: Siem Reap Riverside
blurb: The lit riverbank between the old market and Wat Bo, quiet two streets from Pub Street.

name: Battambang Heritage Walk
blurb: Shophouse rows, a governor's residence and the best-kept French streets in the country.

name: Kampot Riverside
blurb: Sunset boats and a strip of low-key bars along the Praek Tuek Chhu.

name: Phnom Penh Night Market
blurb: Weekend stalls by the river where everyone eats sitting on mats.

name: Angkor Night Market
blurb: The original of the town's night markets, still the best for silk and silver.

name: Sihanoukville Night Market
blurb: Grilled seafood and skewers a block back from the port, busiest around nine.

name: Street 240
blurb: Cafés and small boutiques along the shophouse row behind the Royal Palace.

name: Battambang Café Row
blurb: Third-wave roasters in shophouses, several of them training baristas as social enterprises.

name: Kampot Café Scene
blurb: Riverside and old-town cafés, including a deaf-run arts café that has been here for years.

name: Phnom Penh Rooftop Bars
blurb: The view over the four rivers from the top of the city's newer towers.

name: Siem Reap Rooftops
blurb: Pool decks and terraces above the hotel strip, with the temples dark on the horizon.

name: Russian & Central Markets
nameKh: ផ្សារទួលទំពូង
blurb: The 1937 art-deco dome, and the tighter, hotter aisles of Toul Tom Poung.

name: Psar Chas (Old Market)
blurb: The market the tourist quarter grew around, still selling to locals in the mornings.

name: Kandal Village
blurb: Two streets of designer studios, concept stores and coffee, west of the old market.

name: Psar Nath
blurb: The yellow deco market hall on the riverfront, and the town's actual centre.

name: Battambang Art Scene
blurb: Independent gallery spaces in colonial shophouses, showing work from the arts school up the road.

name: Phare Ponleu Selpak
blurb: The arts school founded by returning refugees in 1994, and the circus that came out of it.

name: Phare, The Cambodian Circus
blurb: Nightly performances under a big top, staged by graduates of the Battambang school.

name: Java Creative Café
blurb: One of the capital's longest-running independent gallery and café spaces.

name: Bassac Lane
blurb: A run of tiny owner-run bars and kitchens off Street 308.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Phnom Penh Food Lanes
blurb: Grilled skewers, num pang and iced coffee from carts that appear at dusk.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Pub Street
blurb: Loud, cheap and unavoidable — with quieter lanes one block either side.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Kep Crab Market at Dusk
blurb: The whole evening in one place: crab, pepper, and the boats coming in behind you.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Kep Crab Market
blurb: Blue swimmer crab, green pepper, and a queue that moves fast.
tips: Ask for mild if you prefer less chilli

name: Prahok Season, Kampong Thom
blurb: Fish paste made in the open each December, and the smell that comes with it.
tips: Ask for mild if you prefer less chilli

name: Num Banh Chok Mornings
blurb: Rice noodles under green fish gravy, sold from baskets before eight in the morning.
tips: Ask for mild if you prefer less chilli

name: Kien Svay Riverside Picnics
blurb: Stilted platforms over the Mekong where families eat grilled fish and sticky rice all afternoon.
tips: Ask for mild if you prefer less chilli

name: Kralan Roadside Stalls
blurb: Sticky rice, coconut and beans grilled inside a bamboo tube and split open at the roadside.
tips: Ask for mild if you prefer less chilli

name: Psar Thmei Food Stalls
nameKh: ផ្សារធំថ្មី
blurb: The 1937 art-deco dome, and the best kuy teav counters are around its edges.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Bai Sach Chrouk Mornings
nameKh: បាយសាច់ជ្រូក
blurb: Grilled pork over broken rice with pickles and a bowl of broth — the standing national breakfast.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Road 60 Night Market
blurb: Where the town actually eats after dark — grills, fairground rides and not a tourist menu in sight.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Skun Market
blurb: The famous fried tarantula stop on the road east — and much better sticky rice.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Russian Market Food Hall
blurb: A dozen stalls wedged into the middle of the market, cooking from seven in the morning.
tips: Busy stalls turn food over fastest

name: Modern Khmer Fine Dining
blurb: Tasting menus rebuilding Khmer dishes from the provinces, several run as training restaurants.

name: Siem Reap Fine Dining
blurb: Kitchens sourcing from the lake and the farms around town, a few streets off the strip.

name: Guide-listed Kitchens, Phnom Penh
blurb: The capital's rooms that appear in international restaurant guides.

name: Guide-listed Kitchens, Siem Reap
blurb: Temple-town kitchens carrying international guide listings, most of them small.

name: Siem Reap Cooking Schools
blurb: Market shop, then amok and prahok ktis in a half-day, in a dozen kitchens around town.
tips: Tell them about allergies when booking

name: Phnom Penh Cooking Classes
blurb: Half-days that start in Psar Thmei and end with samlor korko on the table.
tips: Tell them about allergies when booking

name: Battambang Farm Kitchens
blurb: Cooking in the rice belt, with the vegetables picked in the garden you are standing in.
tips: Tell them about allergies when booking

name: Kampot Pepper Farms
blurb: Protected-origin pepper terraces you can walk, taste and buy at the source.
detail: Pepper has been grown on these slopes since at least the thirteenth century, and the Kampot designation is one of Cambodia's first two protected geographical indications. Most farms are small, trellised plots you can walk through, and the tasting is worth doing properly — black, red and white are the same berry picked and processed differently, and the difference between them is obvious side by side.
tips: Wear shoes you can get muddy

name: Palm Sugar Kilns
blurb: Sugar palms tapped at dawn and boiled down by the roadside all morning.
tips: Wear shoes you can get muddy

name: Battambang Rice Country
blurb: The country's rice bowl, with bamboo sticky rice grilled along the roads out of town.
tips: Wear shoes you can get muddy

name: Rice Wine & Craft Distilleries
blurb: Village sraa sor and the small distilleries infusing it with pepper, ginger and palm sugar.
tips: Wear shoes you can get muddy

name: Siem Reap Organic Farms
blurb: Market gardens outside town supplying the restaurants, most open for a morning visit.
tips: Wear shoes you can get muddy

name: Banteay Chhmar Homestay
nameKh: បន្ទាយឆ្មារ
blurb: Sleep in the village beside a Jayavarman VII temple city, with dinner cooked at the house.

name: Koh Trong Homestays
blurb: Family houses on a Mekong sandbank island, reached by the little ferry from Kratié.

name: Chambok CBET
blurb: One of the country's oldest community projects, with ox-cart rides, a waterfall trail and thirty host families.

name: Sambor Prei Kuk Homestays
nameKh: សំបូរព្រៃគុក
blurb: Village stays beside the pre-Angkorian brick towers, with guiding by people who grew up among them.

name: Areng Valley
blurb: A valley the community kept from being dammed, now open for stays and river trips.
tips: Small notes are easier for change

name: Kampong Phluk Boat Cooperative
nameKh: កំពង់ភ្លុក
blurb: Village-run rowing boats into the flooded forest, rather than the big tour launches.
tips: Small notes are easier for change

name: Trapeang Sangkae
nameKh: ត្រពាំងសង្កែ
blurb: A fishing community that replanted its own mangrove, and now guides boats through it.
tips: Small notes are easier for change

name: Silk Weaving Cooperatives
blurb: Golden-silk weaving villages where the whole chain, worm to cloth, is on one street.

name: Mekong Blue Silk Centre
blurb: A women's development centre weaving raw silk on the far northern Mekong.

name: Andong Russey Pottery Village
nameKh: អណ្ដូងឫស្សី
blurb: Coil-built cooking pots turned by hand and fired in the open, in the province named after them.

name: Angkor Craft Workshops
blurb: Silk, stone and lacquer workshops training apprentices from the villages around town.

name: Community Rice Farms
blurb: Farm stays in the rice belt, with the day's work starting well before the heat.

name: Pepper Smallholder Cooperatives
blurb: Family plots inside the protected-origin zone, selling under a shared cooperative label.

name: Palm Sugar Cooperatives
blurb: Tapping families organised under the geographical indication, boiling sap the same morning it is cut.

name: Elephant Valley Project
blurb: Retired elephants in forest, with Bunong mahouts employed to walk with them.

name: Osoam Cardamom Community Centre
blurb: A village centre deep in the Cardamoms, and the usual base for multi-day walks into the range.

name: Andoung Kraloeng Gibbon Camp
blurb: A Bunong-run forest camp in Keo Seima, and dawn treks to habituated yellow-cheeked gibbons.

name: Prek Toal Community
blurb: Former egg collectors now guard the colony and guide the boats into it.

name: Tmatboey Ibis Site
blurb: A village in Kulen Promtep that protects nesting giant and white-shouldered ibis, and is paid per sighting.
detail: A village of a few hundred families inside Kulen Promtep Wildlife Sanctuary, and the best place in the world to see giant ibis — a bird down to a few hundred pairs, almost all of them in northern Cambodia. The arrangement is direct: the community protects the nests, and visitors pay a conservation contribution on top of the stay, with a bonus paid to the village when a bird is seen. Best from December to May, when the water is down.

name: Ang Trapeang Thmor
blurb: Sarus cranes on a Khmer Rouge-era reservoir, watched from the village that farms around it.

name: Boeung Prek Lapouv
blurb: Grassland on the Vietnamese border holding the country's other sarus crane flock in the dry months.

name: Chi Phat CBET
blurb: The country's best-known community ecotourism project, run by former loggers and poachers.
tips: Agree the route before you set off

name: Yeak Laom Community
blurb: The Tampuan committee that owns and manages the crater lake, and guides around it.
tips: Agree the route before you set off

name: Ta Veng River Guides
blurb: Brao boatmen running the upper Sesan and the northern approach into Virachey.
tips: Agree the route before you set off

name: Siem Reap Boutique Stays
blurb: Small properties in the lanes off Wat Bo, most under thirty rooms and built around a courtyard.

name: Phnom Penh Riverside Hotels
blurb: Colonial-era and contemporary rooms looking over the four-rivers junction.

name: Kep Hillside Villas
blurb: Villas on the slope above the bay, with the crab market ten minutes below.

name: Kampot Riverside Retreats
blurb: Low-key riverside properties with the Bokor range standing behind them.

name: Private Island Retreats
blurb: Whole-island properties in the Koh Rong archipelago, reached by private launch.

name: Inner Island Villas
blurb: Beachfront villas on the closer islands, thirty minutes out rather than two hours.

name: Siem Reap Golf Courses
blurb: Championship courses a few minutes from the temples, playable year round.

name: Phnom Penh Golf Courses
blurb: Full-length courses on the city's northern and western edges, an easy morning from town.

name: Helicopter Tours over Angkor
blurb: Angkor from the air, the only way to read the full plan of the city at once.

name: Island & Coastal Air Transfers
blurb: Charter flights and helicopter hops that turn a six-hour road transfer into forty minutes.

name: Gulf Yacht Charters
blurb: Crewed day and overnight charters out through the archipelago to the outer islands.
tips: Charter prices vary by group size

name: Mekong River Cruises
blurb: Cabin cruises between Phnom Penh, the Tonle Sap and the delta below the border.
tips: Charter prices vary by group size

name: Angkor Private Guiding
blurb: Licensed guides who work from the inscriptions, on your schedule rather than a coach's.

name: Cardamom Naturalist Guiding
blurb: Private guiding with the biologists and rangers who survey the range.

name: Phnom Penh Museum Guiding
blurb: Curator-led mornings in the National Museum, before the tour groups reach it.

name: Phnom Penh Fine Dining
blurb: Modern Khmer tasting menus, several of them run as training restaurants.

name: Siem Reap Fine Dining
blurb: Kitchens sourcing from the lake and the farms around town, a few streets off the strip.

name: Siem Reap Spa Retreats
blurb: Hotel spas built around Khmer massage and herbal compress, most open to non-residents.

name: Cardamom Rainforest Lodges
blurb: Tented camps on the Tatai river that fund the ranger patrols around them.

name: Kampot Wellness Retreats
blurb: Yoga and treatment weeks on the river, usually booked by the week rather than the night.

name: VIP Angkor Access
blurb: Early-access arrangements, private transport and a guide who plans around the light.

name: Northern Temples Expedition
blurb: Preah Vihear, Koh Ker and Preah Khan of Kompong Svay in one private run, with the transport it takes.
